newsitem.title: USA: GM's GMAC $1 bln global debt seen well-bid.
newsitem.headline: GM's GMAC $1 bln global debt seen well-bid.

text.p: General Motors' GMAC $1.0 billion global five-year notes were enveloped in positive sentiments on Wednesday ahead of its formal pricing, according to syndicate officials.

The non-callable notes were said to be well-bid as of midmorning based on price talk of 42 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve. Two syndicate officials not included in the selling group said the deal was perhaps one to two basis points cheap to the market.
The deal is expected to be priced Wednesday morning via co-managers Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and J.P. Morgan Securities.
Demand for the notes was at least in part due to the shorter maturity amid what has become a sea of 10- to 30-year straight corporate issuance and long capital securities.
"There's a lack of supply in the three- to five-year sector," one syndicate manager said. "There's a very big need for these with the recent back-up in rates.
"There's a pent-up demand for the shorter dated stuff and it could come tighter," he added.
Unfazed by the weight of GMAC's $1 billion offer, several other large investment grade deals are expected to capitalize on the powerful corporate market on Wednesday.
--GTE Corp will issue $500 million in 30-year debt at a spread as tight as 95 basis points. The bonds will likely carry a 10-year call feature.
--Eastman Chemical Co will issue $300 million 30-year non-callable bonds at a spread near 80 basis points.
--Baxter International Inc is expected to sell $450 million in 10-year notes and 30-year bonds at spread levels near 50 basis points and 70 basis points, respectively.
--State Development Bank of China will sell $300 million 10-year Yankee notes around a 80 basis point spread.

Capital securities, or trust preferred issues, also continue to queue up ahead of the Clinton Administration's budget proposal. Market participants believe the proposal will include provisions that would eliminate the tax-deductable nature trust preferred dividends.
Issues set to come to market on Wednesday include:
--$300 million 30-year capital securities with a 10-year call feature from Southern Cos and $300 million 30-year bullets from AllAmerica.

Turning to high-yielders, Collins & Aikman Floorcoverings Inc is expected to formally price $100 million 10-year senior subordinated notes via a BT Securities Corp syndicate. At price talk of 10 percent to 10.25 percent, the deal was oversubscribed two days ago, said a source close to the deal.
Also, Vintage Petroleum's $100 million in senior subordinated notes may price on Wednesday.

High-yield issues enjoyed a firm aftermarket on Wednesday, with the exception of Tuesday's exchangeable preferred stock offering from Granite Broadcasting Corp, traders said. The securities were bid at 99 near midday on Wednesday compared with a par issue price.
Orion Network Systems Inc's $710 million senior notes and senior discount notes were bid higher following the late Tuesday pricing.
